module: Module 2: Expert vs Non-Expert Physiological Differentiation
project: MP2026CSE86 - EEG & ECG Analysis of Physiological Differences Associated with Yoga Experience

cohort_overview.expert_criteria: Minimum 3+ consecutive years of daily meditation and asana practice.
cohort_overview.control_criteria: Healthy age-matched non-practitioners with zero prior formal yoga or meditation training.

eeg.layman_summary: In normal individuals, calm waves (Alpha/Theta) only surge when falling asleep, while awake focus produces chaotic Beta waves. In yoga experts, Theta waves stay strong and stable during awake concentration without drifting into drowsiness or anxiety.

ecg.mind_state: Enhanced Vagal Tone & Parasympathetic Stress Resilience
ecg.layman_summary: Normal hearts beat rigidly like metronomes under cognitive demand. Yoga experts display significantly elevated heart rate variability (HF power and RMSSD). When they exhale, the vagal brake activates and heart rate drops smoothly, confirming heightened autonomic recovery.

coupling.layman_summary: Normal individuals have decoupled mental and cardiac states (mind races while heart rests, or vice versa). In yoga experts, diaphragmatic breath control dampens arterial blood pressure swings via the baroreflex, directly driving cortical Theta synchrony. Brain rhythms and cardiac cycles lock into harmonic unison.

eeg_theta_alpha_ratio.physiological_meaning: Inward Meditative Absorption vs Scattered Fluctuations
eeg_theta_alpha_ratio.layman_interpretation: Yoga experts maintain a low, disciplined ratio (4.52) compared to normal individuals (17.62). Normal minds fluctuate heavily with scattered thoughts, whereas experts sustain steady inward absorption without mental fatigue.

eeg_theta_beta_ratio.physiological_meaning: Attentional Regulation vs Cognitive Stress / Anxiety
eeg_theta_beta_ratio.layman_interpretation: Normal people produce erratic Beta wave bursts under focus. Yoga experts maintain a controlled ratio of 27.54, demonstrating that attentional control prevents cognitive stress spikes.

eeg_theta_rel_mean.layman_interpretation: Yoga experts dedicate over 4.3x more of their total cortical brain energy to the serene Theta band (4–8 Hz) even while performing active tasks.

eeg_delta_rel_mean.layman_interpretation: Normal individuals exhibit significantly higher baseline Delta waves (10.07% vs 7.19%), reflecting daytime drowsiness or mental fog compared to alert yogic wakefulness.

eeg_alpha_rel_mean.layman_interpretation: Experts generate 2.4x stronger synchronized Alpha waves (8–13 Hz), keeping the cortex in a relaxed state of ready awareness.

eeg_beta_rel_mean.layman_interpretation: While normal individuals produce scattered Beta bursts, experts demonstrate higher organized cognitive processing efficiency without accompanying anxiety.

ecg_hf.layman_interpretation: The standout cardiac biomarker! Experts possess more than 2.6x higher HF power (79.7 vs 30.3). Slower, diaphragmatic yogic breathing stimulates the vagus nerve directly with every exhale.

ecg_rmssd.readable_name: RMSSD (Root Mean Square of Successive Differences)
ecg_rmssd.layman_interpretation: Experts register an astonishing 91.2 ms vs 49.3 ms in normal people (+85% increase). Higher beat-to-beat variability proves an elastic, healthy heart that effortlessly recovers from stress.

ecg_pnn50.layman_interpretation: More than double in yoga practitioners (20.7% vs 10.3%). Consecutive heartbeats are constantly and fluidly adjusting to respiratory demands.

ecg_lf.layman_interpretation: Experts show 3.1x higher LF power (57.1 vs 18.3), which in trained individuals indicates powerful, rhythmic blood pressure baroreflex resonance during deep breathing.

ecg_sdnn.layman_interpretation: Total heart rate spread is 63.2 ms in experts vs 43.4 ms in normal people (+45%), signifying a broader physiological dynamic range.

coupling_alpha_rmssd_prod.physiological_meaning: Simultaneous Brain Relaxation & Cardiac Vagal Recovery
coupling_alpha_rmssd_prod.layman_interpretation: The single biggest standout in the entire study! Multiplies relaxed Alpha brain waves by cardiac vagal recovery. In experts, when the brain relaxes, the heart instantly mirrors it, resulting in over 10.5x higher synchronization (0.41 vs 0.04).

coupling_neuro_cardiac_index.layman_interpretation: Measures mathematical phase-locking between cortical rhythms and cardiac cycle timing. Experts demonstrate 2.4x higher coherence (1.28 vs 0.53).

coupling_theta_lf_ratio.layman_interpretation: Rhythmic diaphragmatic breathing anchors cardiac autonomic oscillations to hippocampal and frontal Theta waves, producing an integrated mind-body state.
